method.label: Use a common secant root sum

annotationRationale: The factor theorem expresses f(x)-x² using its three known zeros. The cubic root-sum identity then relates all three secant intersections through coefficients unchanged by subtracting a line.
sourceMethod: Followed the official method of subtracting x² and using the unchanged root sum for f(x)-L(x). Introduced the common sum S to make the secant arithmetic explicit.

review.mathCheck: Writing f(x)=x²+a(x−2)(x−3)(x−4) gives the common secant root sum S=9−1/a. Adding the three secant equations yields 3S=18+24=42, hence a=−1/5 and f(0)=24/5, choice D. The third intersection coordinates are 9, 8, and 7, so they are genuinely additional intersections.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, independently phrased adaptation of official solution 23 on page 10: subtract x², factor using the three zeros, and exploit coefficients unchanged by subtracting a line.
review.annotationCheck: The factorization, coefficient signs, secant correspondences, and root-sum calculation are explicit and reconstructable. Both assessed nodes are appropriate.
